memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh's per-extension loop iterates `for ext_path in "$EXT_DIR"/*/`, so ext_path always carries a trailing slash. Any new per-extension check function doing a prefix-strip against `$ext_path/scripts/...` (or any other subdirectory) must normalize with `${ext_path%/}` first, or the strip builds a double-slash prefix that silently never matches `find`'s output, degrading the check to reporting every file in every extension as a false positive. Rules A/H (glob-based) never hit this because a doubled slash is harmless to a glob; any new find-based rule must normalize explicitly.

Rule F (check_deployed_script_drift) in check-extension-docs.sh applies uniformly to every extension including core, treating any deployed-vs-source content mismatch as a hard FAIL -- unlike Rule O (check_core_deploy_advisory), which downgrades a MISSING core deployment to an ADVISORY specifically because forcing a hard FAIL there would brick the gate for every caller until a manual deploy-tree regeneration. Consequence: any source-store edit to check-extension-docs.sh's own file will register as a Rule F self-drift FAIL against the (unregenerated) deployed .claude/scripts/ copy until someone runs the manual regeneration step. This is a structural, currently-undocumented asymmetry between Rule F and Rule O worth knowing before assuming a non-zero doc-lint exit after any core-script edit indicates a defect in the edit itself.
